clue.text: "There is a — greater than the sky, and it is the human soul" (Victor Hugo)

definitions.text: "There is a — greater than the sky, and it is the human soul" (Victor Hugo)

parts.words: "There is a — greater than the sky, and it is the human soul" (Victor Hugo)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: the missing word is the one Hugo used in Les Misérables for a view or vista grander than the sea and the sky

explanation.surface: A line from Victor Hugo comparing the vastness of the soul with the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: Quotation clues are general knowledge: the blank is a noun meaning a wide view or outlook, the word in the standard English translation of Hugo.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide vista or outlook is the sense Hugo's translated sentence needs, the noun for a scene one looks out on.

clue.text: Turns take five around about four

indicators.note: the turned word goes about, round, the Roman numeral for four
turned around, so the letters of the break word are read backwards

parts.note: to take five is to stop for a short break
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone taking a five-minute break at around four o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns the break word backwards and 'about' wraps it round the numeral. The obvious reading takes 'five' as V, but 'take five' is one phrase meaning a short rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To swivel on a fixed point is to rotate or swing round, so the verb works as a synonym for spinning.

clue.text: Work upset abrupt Vedic poet like Jorthkyn

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to go is to work or function, as a machine does

indicators.note: abrupt means cut short, so the poet's final letter is lopped off

parts.note: a rishi is an inspired sage or poet of the Vedic hymns

explanation.surface: Some writing goes wrong for a curt Vedic poet compared to a character called Jorthkyn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses GO to OG in this down entry; 'abrupt' docks the last I of RISHI. Jorthkyn is an ogre in a fantasy novel, so the definition needs an adjective of monstrous brutishness.
explanation.definitionFit: Jorthkyn is a monster from fantasy fiction, so something resembling him is brutish and giant-like.

clue.text: "I have learnt that I am Häftling. My number is 174517." (—)

definitions.text: "I have learnt that I am Häftling. My number is 174517." (—)

parts.words: "I have learnt that I am Häftling. My number is 174517." (—)
parts.note: the blank asks for the author of these words, an Italian chemist's memoir of his Auschwitz prisoner number

explanation.surface: A survivor's flat statement of his identity reduced to a camp prisoner's number.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation comes from If This Is a Man, the Turin chemist's account of Auschwitz; Häftling is German for prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: The quoted lines are from the memoir If This Is a Man, so the blank names the Italian chemist and writer who survived the camp.

clue.text: Best-selling author levels circus in a rage

indicators.note: something in a rage is wild and out of control, so these letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A popular writer flattens a circus while furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a rage' rearranges the twelve letters of LEVELS CIRCUS.
explanation.definitionFit: He wrote the Dirk Pitt adventure thrillers, which sold in vast numbers worldwide.

clue.text: Planet Killer's a book by written two former students

indicators.note: a book written by someone has its author's name first, so the students come before the book

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate
an OB is an old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A book about a planet-destroyer, co-written by two alumni.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Little Prince the hero must uproot the seedlings of a giant tree before their roots split his tiny planet, hence 'Planet Killer'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Saint-Exupéry's fable the African tree's roots threaten to shatter the prince's asteroid, making it a destroyer of worlds.

clue.text: A long introductory part from Hamlet

parts.note: to long for something is to have an itch for it

explanation.surface: A lengthy opening section taken from Shakespeare's tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letter of Hamlet is H, and the definition asks for that letter's name spelt out.
explanation.definitionFit: The word Hamlet begins with H, and the definition wants the spelt-out name of that letter.

clue.text: Boyfriend meeting very old Irish writer

parts.note: a beau is a boyfriend or admirer

explanation.surface: A girlfriend's companion meets an elderly Irish author.
explanation.definitionFit: Simone de Beauvoir was a French author and philosopher, writer of The Second Sex.

clue.text: Bishop pulling a blade gets cut by northern poet

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: a word cut by a letter has that letter slicing into its middle

parts.note: pulling an oar blade through water is rowing

explanation.surface: A churchman drawing a knife is wounded by a poet from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulling a blade' looks like drawing a knife, but the blade is an oar's. 'gets cut by' puts N into ROWING.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Browning was the Victorian author of dramatic monologues such as My Last Duchess.

clue.text: Wake one hugging king and a general's missus

indicators.note: the watch word wraps round the king's letter as a hug encloses someone

parts.note: a wake is a watch kept over the dead, a vigil
R is short for rex, Latin for king
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A mourner at a wake embraces a monarch and a general's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hugging' puts R inside VIGIL. The general is Coriolanus, the Roman soldier of Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's Coriolanus she is the wife of the general, so she is his spouse.

clue.text: Street artist, occasional abbot or Greek geographer

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: taking only now-and-then letters of the next word, its second and fourth

explanation.surface: A street painter, a part-time abbot, or an ancient mapmaker of Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasional' picks the second and fourth letters of ABBOT, giving BO.
explanation.definitionFit: He wrote the Geographica, a vast description of the known world in the first century.

clue.text: The Italian maker of finer fan clad in tatters

indicators.note: torn to rags, so these words' letters are ripped up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A craftsman from Italy makes a fine fan dressed in rags.
explanation.walkthrough: The Italian is a Gothic novel of 1797, so its maker is its author. 'in tatters' rearranges FINER FAN CLAD.
explanation.definitionFit: She wrote the Gothic novel The Italian, so she created that book.

clue.text: Ultimately, poet Busacca is very Italian poet

indicators.note: ultimately points to the closing letter of each of the next three words

parts.note: so means very, as in so good

explanation.surface: A poet named Busacca is thoroughly Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately' takes the last letters of POET, BUSACCA and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Torquato Tasso wrote the epic Jerusalem Delivered in sixteenth-century Italy.

clue.text: Frieda Weekely's one with Lawrence going to warmer place abroad

indicators.note: the novelist's initials move on to join what follows

parts.note: Frieda Weekley was German, and in German one is ein
D H are the initials of Lawrence the novelist, who eloped with Frieda
an oven warms food

explanation.surface: Frieda goes off with Lawrence to somewhere hotter overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: Frieda Weekley left her husband for D. H. Lawrence; she was German, so her 'one' is EIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Eindhoven is a Dutch city, a foreign location for a British reader.

clue.text: Stern courier turned over long-awaited Tolstoy work

indicators.note: turned over means flipped and churned, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A severe messenger handed over a novel by Tolstoy that readers had waited for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned over' rearranges STERN COURIER. The rising of the dead is long-awaited in Christian belief, and the title was Tolstoy's last novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolstoy's final novel bears this title, which also names the rising from the dead believers await.

clue.text: Stab victim nurse holds in a surgical procedure

parts.note: Julius Caesar was stabbed to death on the Ides of March

indicators.note: the nurse's letters hold the a inside them

parts.note: EN is an enrolled nurse

explanation.surface: A nurse keeps a stabbing casualty in an operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds in' puts A inside EN.
explanation.definitionFit: A delivery of a baby by cutting through the abdomen is an operation, named after Julius Caesar.

clue.text: Periodical that's written about jewellery being Ivanovich's vice

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the magazine word is set down backwards

parts.note: a mag is a magazine, a periodical
bling is flashy jewellery

explanation.surface: A magazine article about jewellery reveals a man's weakness.
explanation.walkthrough: Alexei Ivanovich narrates Dostoevsky's The Gambler. 'about' reverses MAG to GAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Dostoevsky's narrator is addicted to roulette, so his besetting sin is betting.

clue.text: Time to probe odd reasons people like Seab Cooley

indicators.note: the time letter probes, or pushes into, the jumbled word
odd means strange, so the letters are arranged unusually

explanation.surface: Time spent investigating strange motives of a man like Seab Cooley.
explanation.walkthrough: Seab Cooley is a Southern politician in Allen Drury's Advise and Consent. 'odd' rearranges REASONS and 'to probe' puts T inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Seab Cooley sits in the US upper chamber in Drury's novel, so those like him are members of it.

clue.text: Reshuffling ideal (else May could become George Osborne's lover)

indicators.note: reshuffling a cabinet moves its members around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A political reshuffle in which Theresa May might become the lover of the Chancellor George Osborne.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on Theresa May and Chancellor George Osborne; the George Osborne meant is the soldier who marries her in Thackeray's Vanity Fair.
explanation.definitionFit: In Vanity Fair the gentle heroine is courted by and marries George Osborne.

clue.text: Rose Aylmer was his girl and original nurse

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the words carry the answer within them

explanation.surface: A poet's sweetheart was also his first nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurse' signals letters held inside GIRL AND ORIGINAL. Rose Aylmer is the title and subject of an elegy by Walter Savage Landor.
explanation.definitionFit: He wrote the famous lyric Rose Aylmer, so the poem belongs to that poet.

clue.text: Fuss about ordinary service for late thinker

indicators.note: the outer letters go about, round, the service's letters

parts.note: ado is fuss, as in much ado
RN, the Royal Navy, is the senior service

explanation.surface: A to-do over an ordinary funeral for a dead philosopher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about': fuss and ordinary together go round the service. Theodor Adorno was a Frankfurt School philosopher who died in 1969; the Royal Navy is called the senior service in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Adorno was a German philosopher, now dead, so he is a deceased intellectual.

clue.text: One delivering a handbag and black frame with little girl

parts.note: B is short for black, as on pencils
a rack is a frame for holding things
Nell is a pet form of Eleanor or Helen

explanation.surface: Someone handing over a bag and a dark frame along with a small girl.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Bracknell, in Wilde's The Importance of Being Earnest, delivers the famous line 'A handbag?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilde's formidable aunt is famous for her incredulous delivery of the line about a handbag.

clue.text: Enthusiastic-sounding Punch illustrator

indicators.note: sounding means the word is heard, so a spelling with the same sound is wanted

parts.note: keen means enthusiastic

explanation.surface: A cartoonist for the magazine Punch who sounds eager.
explanation.walkthrough: Punch was a British humour magazine; Charles Keene drew for it in the Victorian era.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Keene was a Victorian artist whose cartoons appeared in Punch magazine for decades.

clue.text: Note Oliver Twist, for example, could get Pulitzer?

parts.note: A is a note in music
orphan Oliver is a ward of the parish workhouse

explanation.surface: Musing whether a novel like Oliver Twist might win the Pulitzer.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the Pulitzer as one example of a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pulitzer is a prize given for journalism and letters, an example of an honour.

clue.text: Island Boys to cover pieces from operetta Gypsy Princess

indicators.note: the boys word covers, or encloses, the picked letters

parts.note: boys grow into men, and men can mean boys in a team

indicators.note: pieces from means the first letters taken from each of the two words

explanation.surface: Boys from an island cover numbers from the operetta The Gypsy Princess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces from' takes O and G, the first letters of OPERETTA and GYPSY; 'to cover' puts them inside MEN. Imogen is the princess in Shakespeare's Cymbeline.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's Cymbeline she is the king's daughter, so she is royalty.

clue.text: Proposal to take on Bottom or Brutus, perhaps

indicators.note: the proposal takes on, or takes in, the bottom word

parts.note: an offer is a proposal
the end is the bottom of something

explanation.surface: A suggestion to cast someone as Bottom or Brutus in Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottom and Brutus look like a pair of Shakespeare roles, but Bottom means END and only Brutus, Caesar's killer, is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutus joined the murder of Caesar, so he is a wrongdoer or criminal.

clue.text: Try and briefly read out each letter in Wilton Barnhardt work

parts.note: a go is a try

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter goes

parts.note: to spell is to read out a word letter by letter

explanation.surface: Attempt to read out every letter of a novel by Wilton Barnhardt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' docks the last L of SPELL. Gospel is a 1993 novel by Wilton Barnhardt.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnhardt's novel about a search for a lost text is titled after the books of the evangelists.

clue.text: Turtle and lion managed to come round and get on

parts.note: Leo is the lion of the zodiac

indicators.note: coming round means turning about, so the managed word is read backwards

parts.note: ran means managed, as a business
to do is to get on, as in how are you doing

explanation.surface: A turtle and a lion contrive to recover and get along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come round' reverses the managed word. The turtle is one of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, named after the painter.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the four Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles bears the Renaissance painter's name.
